chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Ibrahim ibn al-Khattab, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The bottom part of the wall complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from the weight of its upper part. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed unto it: 'Bear each other's weight'.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the wall metaphor in Shia hadith regarding divine unity?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted as a metaphor for the hierarchical structure of creation and the specific role of the Imams as the foundational support for the rest of the universe. It highlights the concept of *Tawhid* not just as monotheism, but as an interconnected cosmic order where lower entities sustain higher ones through divine decree, reflecting the Shia belief in the spiritual and metaphysical centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moala, from Ibrahim Bin Al Khataab, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The bottom part of the wall complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from the weight of its upper part. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto it bear each other’s weight’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Thaqafiy from Ali ibn al-Mu‘alla’ from Ibrahim ibn al-Khattab in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

The lower parts of the wall complained before Allah because of the weight of the upper parts and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, inspired it saying, ‘Certain parts of you must leave the other parts.’”
